findings.title: New POST body parameter has no caller: ConfigService.set still sends GET to a route that is now POST-only, so saving settings fails
findings.problem: This diff adds an optional JSON `body` to RestService.post, which is the staged frontend half of the config-set GET->POST migration. Nothing in the frontend uses it yet. The backend half is already merged at HEAD (b55339a): src/python/web/handler/config.py:25-28 registers `/server/config/set` only through `add_post_handler`, with no path segments. The frontend still calls `this._restService.sendRequest(url)`, which is a GET, against `/server/config/set/${section}/${option}/${value}` (src/angular/src/app/services/settings/config.service.ts:22 and :68), and still double-URL-encodes the value (:66). Every settings save from the UI will therefore get a 404/405 back, so ConfigService never updates its local config copy. If ConfigService is not switched to `post(CONFIG_SET_URL, {section, option, value})` in this same change, the settings page stays broken. pending: confirm whether the ConfigService migration is planned as a separate commit in this wave. Until it lands, HEAD ships with config set broken.

findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot save any settings in the deployed app until the frontend caller matches the POST-only backend route.

needs_verification.trigger: user edits any setting, e.g. ConfigService.set('general', 'debug', true)
